title: RFL Extension Registry Entry
description: One registered extension, the controlled mechanism by which RFL accumulates capability without modifying the core (spec/06). An entry declares which of the eight extension-point surfaces it extends, its namespaced + versioned identifier, its lifecycle state, and the Principle-3 conformance artifact that makes it mechanically testable. The registry is empty by design at v0.1 (Principle 5: the registry is the post-v1.0 growth path).

namespace.description: Vendor or domain namespace (spec/06 § Namespace rules). Reserved on first-claim for a vendor; Maintainer-assigned for a domain.

namespace_kind.description: A vendor namespace governs its own extensions on first-claim; a domain namespace is cross-vendor and Maintainer-assigned.

name.description: The extension name within its namespace. Must collide with no reserved core token (enforced by validate.py C8).

version.description: The .v<MAJOR> integer (spec/06 § Version semantics). A major bump mints a new identifier; there is no in-place contract mutation.

identifier.description: The resolved canonical identifier ext.<namespace>.<name>.v<MAJOR>. Its consistency with namespace/name/version is a C8 invariant (JSON Schema cannot assert sibling-value equality).

compact_alias.description: Optional rfl-x:<name> short form for the 03 role-tag and auxiliary-name surfaces (spec/06 § Namespace rules).

surface.description: Which of the eight extensible surfaces this entry extends (spec/06 § What is extensible).

lifecycle.description: Exactly one lifecycle state (spec/06 § Deprecation lifecycle). A retired identifier resolves to unknown (rejected).

successor.description: For a deprecated entry superseded by a .v<MAJOR> successor or a core promotion, the successor identifier (a core name or an ext.* id), so live references migrate without a break. Absent for a withdrawal with no successor.

artifact.description: The Principle-3 chapter-required artifact that makes the extension mechanically testable (a primitive's rubric + conformance fixture, a sensor_class's adapter, etc.). Registration without it is rejected at review (spec/06 § What is extensible).

kind.description: The artifact form required by the owning chapter for this surface.

path.description: Repo-relative path to the artifact (e.g. a conformance fixture or adapter file under this entry's extensions/<namespace>/v<MAJOR>/ directory).

description.description: Human-readable motivation and semantics (spec/06 § Registration process step 1).

implementing_organizations.description: Organizations that implement this extension; the spec/06 § Promotion-to-core cross-vendor-adoption evidence (>= 3 to be eligible).

registered.description: ISO-8601 date the extension was registered.

examples.name: pneumatic-grasp

artifact.description: Terminal-postcondition fixture: a compliant pneumatic enclosure secures a deformable target without exceeding its max_contact_force.

examples.description: A pneumatic-hand-specific grasp primitive (spec/06 § Namespace rules illustrative example). Not registered in the live tree; carried here as the schema's worked example.
